reference_uncertainties.uncertainty: Direct ceremonial witnesses, cohabitation, community recognition, correspondence, family-relative evidence, maternal testimony, the reported will statement, and alternative residence histories conflict. The trial court found marriage; the High Court found it unproved. The target appellate resolution is unavailable.

The statutory text and High Court's invocation of section 50 are supplied, but the complete depositions are not. The extent to which individual witnesses satisfy special-knowledge and conduct-expression requirements cannot be independently determined. The provision's expressly specified divorce and criminal-proceeding limitations must not be transferred automatically to this inheritance suit.

The record includes Ram Hari where the surrounding narrative discusses Ram Piari. The maternal-denial evidence can be attributed cautiously without treating the inconsistent spelling as proof of a different person.

Gokal Chand alleged that his money financed acquisitions in Ram Piari's name, while Raj Kumari alleged that her money financed property for Ram Piari. The supplied excerpts do not independently establish either account for all assets.
The two cars received a separate adverse trial finding against the plaintiff. That finding does not establish ownership of every other asset or the ultimate target appellate treatment of the cars.

The parties disputed whether Gokal Chand was governed by Rajput succession custom. Both reported lower-court accounts contain favorable custom-affiliation findings, but the High Court distinguished affiliation from proof of the asserted inheritance preference.

The High Court's negative finding concerns property provided by Raj Kumari as a stranger. The permitted version does not establish an unrestricted husband-over-daughter priority or resolve whether any different estate category would receive different customary treatment.

The High Court reported Hindu-law priority in favor of Parvin Kumari. The applicable underlying succession provisions are not supplied independently, and the reviewing court's acceptance or modification of that conclusion is withheld.

The defendants alleged a will favoring Parvin, while the trial court found the will invalid for lack of testamentary power under customary law. The original will, execution evidence, legal regime finally applicable, and target appellate determination are unavailable.

The claimant alleged that Parvin was his daughter by Ram Piari. The record does not independently establish that paternal connection. Its uncertainty does not erase the maternal relationship on which her inheritance position rests.

reference_uncertainties.issue: Legal consequences of a proven marriage
reference_uncertainties.uncertainty: Even if Gokal Chand's marriage claim were accepted, succession priority would still depend on an applicable legal or customary inheritance rule and the property category to which it extends. The supplied version cannot establish unconditional husband-over-daughter priority.

The permitted narrative reports the trial decree, High Court dismissal, subsequent appeal, and an initial appellate marriage question. It does not provide the target reasoning or disposition. No winning party or final legal effect may be inferred.

reference_limitations: This output is a proposed source-only MODEL item-design audit. It is not audited human gold, an experimental result, a legal certification, or a determination of the actual target appeal.

The audit uses only the supplied question, scope, complete permitted CASE and LAW excerpts, provisional reference, and mechanical quotation flag. No external authorities, evaluated reports, method identities, performance scores, hidden dispositions, or case-memory sources were used.
Every proposed item has equal nominal weight and a binary material-relation criterion. No item gains extra points for incidental dates, witness names, persuasive phrasing, or unsupported specificity.

The proposed set has no target-count justification. Splits were made when source-supported relations could be reported independently, particularly where different actors, evidentiary grounds, funding accounts, judicial stages, or legal conclusions were involved.

The provisional reference's R02 is retained as one direct-ceremony-evidence criterion because the four witnesses and alleged priest are components of the same reported ceremonial evidence. Family recognition likewise permits alternative manifestations of the same brother-in-law relationship rather than requiring separate points for each exhibit.

P27 and P28 have empty old_item_ids because the defendants' express denial of customary-law applicability and alternative personal-property limitation were not independently enumerated in the provisional criteria. Both are added from the permitted originals without retrospectively claiming that an old item already required them.

P13 concerns the will as reported evidence about marriage; P34 concerns the alleged testamentary transfer; P35 concerns the trial court's legal invalidity finding. These independent relations are not interchangeable and do not imply a final finding about the will.

P21 and P22 assess distinct competing source-of-funds accounts. They do not create additional independently proved beneficial-title or purchase-transaction facts. P23 and P24 separately preserve the allegation and trial finding specific to the cars.

P25, P26, P29, P30, P31, P32, and P33 distinguish customary affiliation, the asserted specific priority, historical acceptance of custom, the stranger-property limitation, and the High Court's Hindu-law conclusion. A report cannot satisfy one simply by stating a generic rule that husbands or daughters inherit first.

The source establishes a case-specific connection to Evidence Act section 50 through the High Court's explicit discussion. It does not establish historical applicability of every other supplied LAW excerpt. No stand-alone legal-application item is created for statutes lacking necessary factual predicates.

No separate legal-application obligation requires the target appellate court to endorse the trial court's will-invalidity reasoning or the High Court's Hindu-law conclusion. Their accurate historical attribution is independently scoreable; current appellate legal effect remains unresolved.

P40 is a single OPEN item for the withheld appellate resolution. It is not a second score for every underlying marriage, custom, property, or testamentary uncertainty and does not require a hidden target outcome.

The original judgment excerpts report allegations, testimony summaries, and earlier judicial findings. Original marriage exhibits, correspondence, school registers, property records, depositions, and testamentary instruments were not independently available.

The original failure arose from intervening citation markup, not from a demonstrated false legal proposition. Other proposed witnesses retain the provided source spellings and line-break artifacts rather than silently normalizing them.

The evidence quotations are short source witnesses, not substitutes for the complete procedural and evidentiary context. A report may satisfy a binary item through accurate paraphrase or equivalent material relations without reproducing the quotation.
